answer: One defense is a bonded entry toll each agent must forge before it can trade or vote: it locks a fixed sum of scarce capital that is slashed on misbehavior. An honest agent pays once and amortizes the cost like slowly growing a single pearl, but a sybil operator must forge a separate bond for every fake identity, so attacker cost scales linearly with the clone count. There is no velvet shortcut: capital cannot be conjured from nothing, making mass fake accounts economically ruinous while genuine agents barely feel it.
